title: 12 Best Hybrid Conference Platforms for B2B Event Teams | Zuddl Blog
summary: Compare 12 hybrid conference platforms on streaming quality, onsite check-in, and CRM integration. Strengths, gaps, pricing, and best-fit scenarios for each
body_markdown:
Your keynote speaker is live on stage in front of 400 people. Three hundred virtual attendees are watching a stream that is running 45 seconds behind. The in-room moderator takes questions from raised hands. The virtual Q&A queue fills up with no one monitoring it. By the time a sales rep checks the CRM two days later, half the virtual attendees have no engagement data attached to their records at all.


A hybrid conference platform manages more than a video stream alongside an in-person event. It coordinates onsite logistics and virtual production, two attendee data streams, and the CRM sync layer connecting both to pipeline. The platform determines whether your sales team gets a single attendee profile with full engagement context or two disconnected spreadsheets.


This article evaluates 13 platforms across streaming quality, onsite check-in, and CRM integration depth. Each entry covers what the platform does well, where it has gaps, pricing, and the team situation it fits best.

## The 12 best hybrid conference platforms for B2B event teams


### Zuddl


Zuddl is the AI-native unified events platform that operates hybrid conferences from a single codebase covering registration, onsite operations, virtual production, and CRM attribution. It serves B2B event teams running conferences, field events, and webinars who need one platform their marketing ops team can configure without developer support.


**What it does well**


- The built-in production studio includes a[scene builder, live and simulive streaming modes, presenter backstage, overlay and lower-thirds controls, and 1-click speaker magic links](https://www.zuddl.com/platform/virtual-and-hybrid-events/video-production-and-streaming) , delivering broadcast-quality hybrid sessions without relying on third-party RTMP tools or external AV production.


- Onsite operations cover[printer support for on-demand badge printing, self-serve kiosks, QR-code session scanning with access control by ticket tier, and offline functionality](https://www.zuddl.com/platform/onsite-events/event-check-in-and-badge-printing) when venue WiFi drops. Zuddl acts as the single point of contact for arranging all onsite equipment including badges, lanyards, printers, iPads, stands, and routers.


- Native bidirectional integrations with Salesforce, HubSpot, Marketo, Eloqua, and Pardot sync detailed attendee statuses (invited, registration abandoned, registered, attended) in real time with retry logic, integration logs, and field-level mapping flexibility. Real-time Slack alerts notify sales reps when target accounts register or check in, surfacing Salesforce fields like Lead ID, Opportunity, and Account Name directly in the alert.


- Complete event configurations, including registration flows, CRM field mappings,[email sequences](https://www.zuddl.com/platform/event-registration-and-ticketing-software/event-communications) , landing page branding, and session structure, can be deep-cloned so recurring conference series or multi-city roadshows launch from an inherited playbook rather than a blank canvas.


- A pre-launch QA agent scans the entire event setup before publish for broken links, missing triggers, unconnected integrations, and misconfigured logic. After the event, an[AI follow-up agent DMs each assigned sales rep in Slack](https://www.zuddl.com/event-integrations) with contact summaries, engagement highlights, and pre-drafted outreach messages, escalating to sales managers when SLA slips.


**Where it has gaps**


- Pricing starts at $10,000/year for the Digital License (minimum two organizer licenses), which can create budget friction for teams anchored to sub-$6,000 point solutions with grandfathered pricing.


**Pricing:** Per-organizer annual pricing. Digital License from $10,000/year (minimum 2 organizer licenses). Unified License (All Events) from $12,000/year.[See pricing](https://www.zuddl.com/pricing)


**Ratings:** 4.8/5 on G2 · 4.5/5 on Capterra


**Best for:** B2B event teams running conferences, field events, and webinars on one unified platform where registration, onsite ops, virtual production, CRM sync, and pipeline attribution share a single data layer, eliminating the multi-tool reconciliation that delays post-event sales follow-up.


### Cvent


Cvent is a category-established event management platform with deep onsite conference capabilities, including its OnArrival check-in system and Attendee Hub for hybrid engagement. It serves large enterprise event teams running multi-thousand-attendee conferences who often need venue sourcing alongside event technology.


**What it does well**


- Onsite check-in and on-demand badge printing are among Cvent's strongest capabilities per reviewer consensus, with successful deployments cited at conferences of 500 to 5,000+ attendees that eliminated morning registration queues.


- Dynamic registration with conditional attendee paths allows event teams to tailor agendas, content, and programming for multiple audience types from a single registration configuration.


- Salesforce campaign integration is cited by enterprise reviewers as one of Cvent's strongest integration points, with registration and attendance data flowing into Salesforce campaigns reliably.


- Attendee Hub connects attendees to event content, networking, and sponsors before, during, and after the event across both web and mobile, with AI-powered networking recommendations for large conferences.


**Where it has gaps**


- CRM sync operates on batch schedules rather than in real time. Multiple reviewers across G2 and Capterra describe sales teams receiving leads 24 to 48 hours after the event ends.


- In-person and virtual engagement data are not automatically merged into a single attendee profile. Reviewers describe spending significant post-event time reconciling two data sets manually.


- Speaker management workflows require manual email coordination rather than a self-serve portal. Reviewers describe chasing asset submissions through email rather than through a dedicated speaker interface.


- No reviewer or vendor evidence of a pre-launch QA agent, AI-assisted event creation, or AI follow-up agent for post-event sales outreach.


**Pricing:** Custom pricing; not listed publicly.


**Ratings:** 4.3/5 on G2 · 4.5/5 on Capterra


**Best for:** Large enterprise conference teams with established procurement relationships who need venue sourcing, scaled onsite badge printing, and Salesforce campaign integration, and whose sales teams can absorb 24 to 48 hour post-event lead delivery delays.


### vFairs


vFairs is a hybrid conference platform with a distinctive 3D virtual environment layer that creates immersive exhibit halls, auditoriums, and customizable virtual venues alongside in-person event operations. It fits trade show and expo organizers who need visual virtual presence alongside onsite logistics.


**What it does well**


- 3D virtual environments with customizable venues, exhibit halls, and auditoriums create an immersive virtual layer that reviewers consistently cite as a standout differentiator for trade shows and expos.


- Exhibitor booth portal allows sponsors to self-customize their virtual presence without event team involvement, with exhibitor analytics and lead capture tools that reviewers praise as among vFairs' strongest features.


- Abstract and call-for-papers management with submission review and approval workflows serves academic and professional conference use cases that many hybrid platforms do not address.


- Registration forms support conditional logic, unlimited ticket types with tiered pricing, and payment capture through Stripe and PayPal, with white-labeled apps available on custom domains.


**Where it has gaps**


- Streaming relies on third-party tools rather than a native broadcast production suite. No scene builder, lower-thirds, presenter backstage, or simulive capability is confirmed on vendor pages or in reviews.


- CRM sync is not real-time. Multiple reviewers report data arriving post-event rather than during the event. Field-level mapping requires vFairs support team involvement, and native Slack integration for sales triggers is absent.


- Q&A and polling are not unified between in-person and virtual audiences. Multiple reviewers report that moderators must manage two separate queues.


- No evidence of event series cloning, deep-clone of CRM field mappings, or series-level analytics for multi-event programs.


**Pricing:** Custom pricing; not listed publicly.


**Ratings:** 4.7/5 on G2 · 4.8/5 on Capterra


**Best for:** Trade show and expo organizers who need immersive 3D virtual exhibit halls alongside in-person badge printing, and whose exhibitor self-service booth customization requirements outweigh the need for real-time CRM sync or broadcast-grade production tools.


### PheedLoop


PheedLoop is a modular hybrid conference platform with built-in streaming, wireless badge printing, and a pay-per-user pricing structure that scales with event size. It serves mid-size conference organizers who want granular control over which capabilities they pay for.


**What it does well**


- Built-in RTMP ingest starts streaming within seconds to thousands of attendees, with a SimuLive feature for pre-recorded content playback and white-labeled Zoom streaming options.


- Wireless badge printing receives repeated praise from reviewers as a standout feature that works reliably in live event environments, and QR-based check-in and session scanning reduce queue times at registration desks.


- The mobile app (iOS and Android) covers gamification, polls, meeting booking, wireless badge printing triggers, and push notifications in a single attendee-facing interface.


- Unlimited speakers and exhibitors per event with over 30 options combining in-person and virtual technologies for sponsors and exhibitors, including gamified badge scanning that drives exhibitor engagement.


**Where it has gaps**


- CRM connectivity relies on Zapier and open API only. No native bidirectional Salesforce or HubSpot integration is confirmed, and multiple reviewers flag that Zapier workarounds introduce sync delays and inconsistent lead attribution.


- Streaming production tools lack advanced scene-building, lower-thirds overlays, or presenter backstage capabilities. Some reviewers report RTMP-based latency that is noticeable during real-time interaction between in-person and virtual attendees.


- Pipeline attribution connecting event attendance to CRM opportunity movement is not native. Multi-event ROI comparison and series-level analytics are not confirmed.


- No evidence of AI-assisted workflow capabilities: pre-launch QA agent, AI follow-up agent, or natural language event creation.


**Pricing:** Starting from $1.75/user/module; mobile event app from $450; $1,000 base platform fee for under 500 user credits.


**Ratings:** 4.8/5 on G2 · 4.7/5 on Capterra


**Best for:** Mid-size conference organizers who want modular pay-as-you-go pricing with strong wireless badge printing and onsite session scanning, and whose CRM integration needs can be handled through Zapier or custom API development.


### Accelevents


Accelevents is a hybrid conference platform with drag-and-drop registration, a native streaming studio, and onsite check-in tools including self-serve kiosks, QR scanning, and RFID. It serves growing conference programs that need onsite operational depth without enterprise-tier pricing.


**What it does well**


- Onsite check-in covers self check-in kiosks, QR scanning, RFID, offline mode, and real-time attendance tracking. Reviewers consistently praise QR code check-in speed and the iPad kiosk setup as easy to deploy, with on-demand badge printing reducing pre-event prep work.


- Drag-and-drop website builder supports separate registration flows for virtual, onsite, and hybrid audiences with advanced forms including custom fields and conditional logic.


- Exhibitor lead capture tools are effective for sponsors to self-manage, with automated sponsor communication workflows that reduce manual follow-up by event teams.


- AI-driven matchmaking and networking features are frequently cited by reviewers as a standout for multi-day conferences.


**Where it has gaps**


- The native studio lacks advanced production features like scene transitions and lower-thirds branding according to multiple reviewers. Streaming integrations rely on third-party pass-through (Zoom, YouTube, Wistia) for high-stakes productions.


- CRM sync is not real-time. Multiple reviewers describe batch or manual post-event data exports. No native Marketo or Pardot integration is documented, and field-level mapping flexibility is flagged as limited.


- No dedicated speaker portal for self-serve asset submission is found on the vendor product page. Reviewer themes confirm speaker materials still route through the event team.


**Pricing:** Professional starting from $5,000/year; Business starting from $12,000/year; Enterprise and White Label plans require a custom quote.


**Ratings:** 4.7/5 on G2 · 4.7/5 on Capterra


**Best for:** Growing B2B conference programs that need strong onsite check-in with offline mode and RFID support at a published annual price point, and whose streaming production needs stay within the capability of a basic native studio supplemented by Zoom or YouTube.


### EventMobi


EventMobi is a modular event management platform covering registration, a branded mobile event app, onsite check-in, badge printing, and hybrid streaming. It serves conference teams that want transparent per-badge pricing and prioritize the attendee app experience.


**What it does well**


- The branded mobile event app with a dedicated CMS (Experience Manager) receives consistent praise from reviewers for attendee engagement, networking, and live polling across both in-person and virtual audiences.


- On-demand badge printing and onsite check-in workflows are described by reviewers as smooth and effective at reducing queues, with 24/7 support including onsite options during live events.


- Unified networking with appointment booking works for both in-person and virtual attendees from within the same platform, facilitating cross-audience meeting scheduling.


**Where it has gaps**


- Live streaming relies on EventMobi Studio powered by Restream, a third-party dependency. No native scene builder, presenter backstage, lower-thirds overlays, or simulive mode is confirmed.


- Reviewers flag limited native integrations with Salesforce and HubSpot, with workarounds required for bidirectional sync and real-time data flows. No evidence of field-level CRM mapping, sync monitoring, or Slack alerts.


- Post-event analytics are not granular enough at the session level according to reviewers, and merging in-person and virtual engagement data into a single attendee profile requires manual effort.


- No evidence of event series cloning, deep-clone of CRM configurations, or series-level analytics.


**Pricing:** Starts at $3.99 per badge; pay-per-event or annual subscription options available; no setup fees, seat fees, or hidden fees.


**Ratings:** 4.6/5 on G2 · 4.7/5 on Capterra


**Best for:** Conference teams that want a modular pay-per-badge pricing model with a strong branded mobile event app and reliable onsite badge printing, and whose streaming production can work through a Restream-powered studio.


### Webex Events & Webinars


Webex Events is Cisco's enterprise hybrid event platform supporting multi-track conferences, trade shows, and networking events at scale up to 100,000 attendees. It fits organizations already standardized on Cisco infrastructure that need hybrid event capabilities within their existing technology ecosystem.


**What it does well**


- Scale to 100,000 attendees with real-time translation in 100+ languages and live simultaneous audio interpretation, serving global enterprise conferences with multilingual audiences.


- Slido integration and six different polling and Q&A types provide interactive engagement tools that reviewers cite as effective for keeping both virtual and in-person audiences participating during sessions.


- Immersive share allows panelists to overlay their camera video on shared content for a broadcast-style presentation format.


**Where it has gaps**


- CRM and marketing automation integrations (Salesforce, HubSpot) are described by reviewers as less native than dedicated event platforms, with workarounds required for bidirectional data flows.


- No native scene builder, simulive mode, presenter backstage, or lower-thirds overlay tooling is confirmed on vendor product pages.


- Onsite check-in and badge printing are confirmed as capabilities, but reviewers describe them as functional rather than polished, with limited self-serve kiosk options.


- No evidence of event cloning, series management, or playbook inheritance functionality. No AI-assisted workflow capabilities found.


**Pricing:** Custom pricing; not listed publicly.


**Ratings:** 4.6/5 on G2 · Not available on Capterra


**Best for:** Large enterprises already running on Cisco infrastructure that need hybrid conference scale to 100,000 attendees with real-time multilingual support, and whose event teams can work within the Webex ecosystem for CRM and production tooling.


### RingCentral Events


RingCentral Events (formerly Hopin) is a virtual-first event platform with hybrid and onsite capabilities, including registration, streaming, check-in, badge printing, and AI-powered content tools. It serves event teams that value transparent per-organizer pricing with unlimited events.


**What it does well**


- Transparent per-organizer pricing starting at $99/organizer/month with unlimited events and registrations gives budget-conscious teams a predictable cost model that reviewers praise versus per-event or per-attendee pricing alternatives.


- Studio-quality streams with backstage access and slide options provide professional virtual production for webinars and hybrid sessions, scaling to 100,000+ attendees.


- AI-powered Smart Content Generator, Smart Q&A categorization, and Smart Clips for generating social media video content from event recordings serve post-event marketing repurposing.


**Where it has gaps**


- Onsite check-in and badging tools are described by reviewers as less mature than virtual-first capabilities, feeling bolted on rather than native, and requiring additional hardware coordination.


- CRM integration sync with HubSpot, Marketo, and Salesforce is described by reviewers as functional but lacking real-time depth. Field mapping flexibility and sync monitoring require manual verification.


- Speaker and sponsor management tools are described as limited for large events. Self-serve portals and sponsor lead capture customization are noted as areas needing improvement compared to dedicated event platforms.


- Multiple reviewers express concern about platform direction following the acquisition by RingCentral, citing uncertainty about long-term feature commitment to event-specific development.


**Pricing:** From $99/organizer/month (Events Pro, annual); Events Pro+ $199/organizer/month; Events Enterprise $299/organizer/month.


**Ratings:** 4.5/5 on G2 · 4.5/5 on Capterra


**Best for:** Event teams running frequent virtual-dominant programs with occasional hybrid components who need transparent per-organizer pricing with unlimited events, and whose post-event content repurposing for social media is a priority workflow.


### Airmeet


Airmeet is a virtual-first event platform with hybrid capabilities and a strong emphasis on attendee networking features like speed networking and social lounges. It serves teams running webinars and mid-size hybrid conferences where virtual attendee engagement is the primary success metric.


**What it does well**


- Networking features, including speed networking (1:1), breakout rooms, social lounges, and sponsored booths, are consistently praised by reviewers as a genuine differentiator that creates attendee connections other platforms do not facilitate.


- Live, simulive, and on-demand webinar support with capacity for up to 100,000 participants and multilingual closed captions and transcripts.


- 24/7 customer support responsiveness during live events is frequently cited as a confidence builder by first-time enterprise event organizers.


**Where it has gaps**


- Onsite and hybrid capabilities feel less mature than virtual-only features. Reviewers managing in-person components report that the physical event layer requires more workarounds. No native badge printing (Zebra/Brother), self-serve kiosks, offline functionality, or equipment fulfillment is confirmed.


- CRM integration depth and reliability are flagged by reviewers. Integrations with Salesforce and HubSpot can be inconsistent, with sync delays or manual reconciliation required post-event.


- Production and streaming customization is limited compared to dedicated broadcast tools. Reviewers seeking scene builder controls, lower-thirds, or branded overlays find the offering insufficient.


**Pricing:** Premium Webinars starting at $167/month (billed annually) for up to 100 attendees. Virtual Events and All-in-Suite plans at custom pricing. Pricing is based on live attendees per event, not total registrations.


**Ratings:** 4.6/5 on G2 · 4.4/5 on Capterra


**Best for:** B2B marketing teams running virtual-dominant programs with a hybrid overlay who prioritize attendee networking and speed networking as the primary engagement mechanism, and whose onsite operations can be handled by a separate logistics provider.


### Swapcard


Swapcard is a hybrid event platform with AI-powered networking and matchmaking as its core differentiator, achieving 70%+ event app adoption rates and claims of 2.5 times more qualified leads compared to manual networking methods. It serves trade shows, association conferences, and media companies where exhibitor ROI and attendee-to-attendee connection drive event value.


**What it does well**


- AI-powered networking with intelligent matchmaking based on attendee profiles, activities, interests, and real-time behavioral signals is the most-praised feature category in reviews, with reviewers reporting attendees forming connections they would not have found manually.


- The Sherlock AI Event Assistant delivers personalized recommendations for speakers, sessions, exhibitors, and attendees, and the Smart Meeting Generator creates speed networking with AI-based meeting matching.


- Badge scanning onsite combined with engagement data qualifies leads and identifies buying behavior, with exhibitor and sponsor lead capture tools well-regarded for facilitating meeting scheduling and follow-up.


**Where it has gaps**


- No native broadcast studio layer (scene builder, simulive, backstage, overlay tools) is confirmed. Streaming appears to rely on integration with external tools.


- CRM integrations require manual post-event data work according to multiple reviewers. No vendor evidence of native bidirectional Salesforce or HubSpot sync with retry logic, field-level mapping, or Slack alerts.


- Onsite check-in and badging is seen as less mature. Multiple reviewers report supplementing Swapcard's native badge printing with external setups at high-volume events.


- Backend event setup and admin configuration are described as complex and not intuitive by reviewers, with a steep learning curve for first-time users.


**Pricing:** Custom pricing; not listed publicly.


**Ratings:** 4.6/5 on G2 · 4.3/5 on Capterra


**Best for:** Trade show and association conference organizers where AI-powered attendee matchmaking and exhibitor lead qualification are the primary value drivers, and whose teams can invest in the admin configuration learning curve and supplement onsite badging independently.


### Whova


Whova is a hybrid conference platform with particular strength in its mobile event app, community-building features, and attendee engagement tools for professional and academic conferences. It serves organizers who prioritize attendee networking, personalized agendas, and community boards over production-grade streaming or deep CRM integration.


**What it does well**


- The mobile event app and engagement features, including community boards, direct messaging, attendee profiles, discussion forums, live polling, and session Q&A, are consistently rated as Whova's standout strength across both G2 and Capterra with high review volumes.


- Passport Contest gamification encourages exhibitor exploration by incentivizing attendees to visit booths and complete activities.


- Automatic attendee type assignment differentiates between in-person and remote attendees with session access control, managing which sessions each audience type can access.


**Where it has gaps**


- No native broadcast-grade production tools. Multiple reviewers confirm dependency on Zoom or external RTMP streams for video production, reducing branding control during hybrid sessions.


- No native Salesforce, HubSpot, Marketo, or Pardot integration is confirmed on vendor pages. Multiple reviewers flag CRM sync as requiring manual CSV export or Zapier with 24+ hour delays.


- Badge printing is not natively supported. Multiple reviewers note it requires a third-party solution or pre-printed badges, and self-serve kiosk check-in is not available.


- No event cloning, series-level analytics, or cross-event comparison dashboards are confirmed. Recurring conference organizers describe rebuilding configurations from scratch each event cycle.


**Pricing:** Custom pricing; not listed publicly.


**Ratings:** 4.8/5 on G2 · 4.8/5 on Capterra


**Best for:** Academic and professional conference organizers running single recurring events where the mobile app, community boards, and attendee networking drive satisfaction scores, and whose teams handle CRM sync manually and source badge printing separately.


### Canapii


Canapii is a hybrid conference platform with registration, a white-label mobile app, live streaming, badge printing, self-service kiosks, and AI matchmaking at an accessible entry price. It serves smaller conference teams running events up to 300 attendees who want a single platform without assembling multiple tools.


**What it does well**


- Registration covers custom forms, conditional pathways, promo codes, and waitlists, with white-label branding across registration pages, emails, and badges.


- Badge printing with self-service kiosks and staffed check-in desks, plus a native event app with offline access, provides onsite operational coverage in a single platform.


- Reviewers consistently praise the hands-on support team, noting assistance through live event execution.


**Where it has gaps**


- The review base is thin (19 Capterra reviews, no G2 reviews), limiting confidence in the reliability of capability claims beyond what the vendor product pages state.


- No native scene builder, simulive mode, presenter backstage, or lower-thirds overlays are documented. Streaming appears to cover standard broadcast without production-grade tooling.


- Integration depth with Salesforce, HubSpot, and Marketo is claimed but not verified for bidirectional real-time sync, field-level mapping, or Slack-based sales alerts.


**Pricing:** Free plan available. Essential plan starts at $2,950 for up to 300 attendees. Professional and Enterprise plans are custom-quoted.


**Ratings:** Not available on G2 · 4.4/5 on Capterra


**Best for:** Smaller B2B conference teams running events of 300 or fewer attendees who need registration, badge printing, and a branded mobile app in one platform at an accessible entry price, and whose CRM and production needs are straightforward.


### Zoom Events


Zoom Events extends the familiar Zoom video infrastructure into multi-day, multi-track virtual and hybrid event management with registration, ticketing, and an event lobby. It serves teams already using Zoom who need virtual event capabilities without switching platforms, though in-person event operations require entirely separate tooling.


**What it does well**


- The familiar Zoom interface eliminates onboarding friction for hosts and attendees. Reviewers consistently cite existing Zoom familiarity as removing barriers to participation.


- Reliable HD video stability and audio quality receive consistent praise across large-scale webinars and virtual events with minimal technical failures.


- Interactive engagement features including polling, live Q&A, reactions, and breakout rooms keep virtual audiences active during sessions.


**Where it has gaps**


- No native onsite check-in, badge printing, QR session scanning, kiosk support, or offline mode. Multiple reviewers confirm that in-person or hybrid events require entirely separate tools for physical event operations.


- No native CRM integration with Salesforce, HubSpot, Marketo, or Pardot is documented on vendor pages. Reviewer themes consistently cite Zapier as the only workaround for CRM data flows.


- Branding and customization are constrained. Reviewers note that adding a logo is possible but the experience still looks and feels like a Zoom event, with limited deep brand customization.


- No event cloning, series management, or playbook inheritance functionality. No evidence of unified in-person and virtual engagement data merging.


**Pricing:** Subscription plans starting at approximately $500/month; annual licenses from approximately $890 to $32,400+ depending on attendee capacity; pay-per-attendee starting at $2.50/person with bulk discounts.


**Ratings:** 4.5/5 on G2 · 4.6/5 on Capterra


**Best for:** Teams already committed to Zoom whose hybrid conference "hybrid" means streaming Zoom sessions at a venue, and who are willing to manage onsite operations, badge printing, and CRM sync through entirely separate tools.


## What to look for in hybrid conference platforms for B2B event teams


**Hybrid streaming and production quality:** Evaluate whether the platform streams in-person sessions through a native studio with scene builder, simulive, and backstage controls, or passes video through RTMP to a third-party tool. Third-party dependencies break branding control and disconnect streaming engagement data from your analytics layer.


**Onsite check-in, badging, and session management:** Confirm[native badge printing with specific printer support, self-serve kiosks, QR session scanning, and offline mode](https://www.zuddl.com/platform/onsite-events/session-management) . Platforms that rely on a separate check-in app create a data silo where onsite attendance does not update CRM status until after the event.


**CRM and marketing automation integration:** Test whether sync is real-time and bidirectional with field-level mapping, or batch-delayed and rigid. When CRM sync runs on a batch schedule, sales reps receive leads 24 to 48 hours after intent has cooled, and sync failures go undetected without monitoring and retry logic.


**Registration experience and pre-event setup:** Check for a[unified registration flow serving both in-person and virtual attendees from one builder with conditional branching](https://www.zuddl.com/platform/event-registration-and-ticketing-software/event-flow-builder) . Separate forms create split attendee records, broken CRM attribution, and inconsistent branding across audience types.


**Speaker, sponsor, and exhibitor management:** Look for[self-serve portals where speakers submit assets and sponsors configure their own lead capture criteria](https://www.zuddl.com/platform/event-speaker-and-exhibitor-portal) . Without these, the event team becomes the bottleneck for every submission, badge scan question change, and team member access request.


**Program setup reuse and event cloning:** Verify whether cloning copies the full configuration, including CRM field mappings, email sequences, and session access rules, or only the landing page layout. Partial cloning compounds into weeks of rework across a multi-event roadshow series.


**Attendee experience and cross-audience engagement** : Test whether in-person and virtual attendees participate in the same Q&A queue, the same polls, and the same networking layer. If virtual attendees submit questions that moderators treat as secondary, they experience the event as a webcast and disengage.


**Unified analytics and pipeline attribution:** Confirm whether[session-level engagement data from badge scans and virtual watch time merge into one attendee profile with CRM attribution](https://www.zuddl.com/platform/event-analytics) . When two systems track two audiences, the post-event team spends weeks reconciling spreadsheets before producing an ROI number.


**AI-assisted event workflow:** Check for pre-launch QA that catches broken integrations before event day, and post-event follow-up automation that distributes contacts with engagement context to sales reps. Without these, configuration errors surface during the live check-in rush and high-intent contacts go cold while reps deprioritize CSV exports.


## Questions people ask about hybrid conference platforms


**What is the difference between a hybrid conference platform and a virtual conference platform?**


A virtual conference platform manages streaming, engagement, and registration for remote-only audiences. A hybrid conference platform adds native onsite operations (badge printing, check-in kiosks, QR session scanning) and merges in-person and virtual attendee data into one engagement profile and CRM record. Platforms without native onsite tools require separate systems that fragment attendee data.


**What features should a hybrid event platform have?**


Core requirements include unified registration serving both audience types from one builder, native streaming with production controls, onsite check-in with badge printing, bidirectional real-time CRM sync, and a single analytics layer that merges in-person and virtual engagement. Zuddl, Cvent, and PheedLoop each cover onsite and virtual in one platform, though their CRM integration depth and production tooling differ significantly.


**How can a hybrid event platform support networking between in-person and virtual attendees?**


The platform needs a shared engagement layer where both audiences access the same Q&A queue, polls, chat, and 1:1 meeting scheduling. Zuddl merges in-person and virtual attendees into one experience with unified Q&A, polls, and two-way speaker conversation. Swapcard uses AI-powered matchmaking. Airmeet offers speed networking and social lounges. The gap to evaluate is whether virtual attendees participate as equals or experience a secondary webcast.


**What integrations should a hybrid conference platform have?**


At minimum: native bidirectional sync with Salesforce, HubSpot, or Marketo that passes detailed attendee statuses in real time. Look for field-level mapping flexibility, sync monitoring with retry logic, and webhooks or open API for non-standard architectures. Platforms that require Zapier workarounds introduce 24+ hour sync delays and unreliable lead attribution that compromise post-event sales follow-up.
